question.text: Malabar Growth Fund (Category II AIF) seeks SEBI prior approval to invest USD 50 million in an offshore technology venture. Under SEBI's guidelines on overseas investment by AIFs/VCFs, which of the following limits apply?

answer.text: Overall cumulative cap of USD 1,500 million across all AIFs, first-come-first-served; the AIF's own overseas allocation cannot exceed 25% of its investable funds
No overall cap; AIF may invest up to 100% of corpus overseas
Each AIF can invest up to USD 500 million on its own; no SEBI approval needed
Only Category III AIFs may invest overseas; Cat II cannot

explanation.text: The Logic: Overseas investment by AIFs is subject to an overall cumulative cap of USD 1,500 million across all AIFs, allocated on a first-come-first-served basis, with SEBI prior approval valid for six months. Each AIF's overseas allocation cannot exceed 25% of its investable funds, the investee must have an Indian connection, and investments cannot be made in restricted/FATF high-risk jurisdictions. The Trap: Option B invents 'no cap'. Option C bypasses SEBI approval. Option D incorrectly excludes Cat II. The 25%-of-investable-funds limit is often overlooked. Note: Workbook pages 380-381 contain the overseas-investment cap and the 25% limit; pages 344-346 support the foreign-investment and jurisdiction constraints.
